text.p: These are leading stories in Pakistani newspapers o8 percent and a fall in national savings are some of the striking features of the national economy during 1995/96 (July-June).
- The State Bank of Pakistan incurred a huge loss of 11.2 billion rupees on account of exchange risk cover provided on foreign currency deposits during fiscal 1995/96 (July/June).

- Pakistan's total national debt stood at 1912.2 billion rupees or 88 percent of its gross domestic product at the end of fiscal year 1995/96 and debt servicing accounted for 63.2 percent of its total tax receipts.
- Pakistan's Jamaat-i-Islami party said on Thursday it would go ahead with its plans to hold a massive sit-in before parliament as part of its campaign against Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.
- Pakistani police said they had arrested 11 policemen in connection with the killing of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza.
- Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban movement has refused to welcome a United States envoy to Kabul because of concern that the group be branded pro-American.
- Pakistan will gradually remove trade barriers with India on the way to granting it most favoured nation status by the year 2000, Commerce Minister Ahmed Mukhtar said on Thursday.
- Various trade organisations in the country have supported the strike call given by the Federation of Pakistan Chamber of Commerce and Industry to protest against new taxes worth 13 billion rupees.
- A high-level delegation of the International Monetary Fund is expected to arrive in Pakistan on Saturday to review the government's economic package announced on Tuesday.
- The World Bank and the Asian Development Bank have taken a serious view of the Pakistan government's failure to disinvest from the two state-owned gas utility companies.
